readerTitle: When a business is worth more on its own
caseNote: 실제 기업 (PepsiCo→Tricon/Yum! Brands, eBay→PayPal) + 가상 사례 두 개 (레스토랑 그룹의 소스 사업, 미용실 예약 소프트웨어의 결제 도구) + 가상 적용 (프로젝트 관리 소프트웨어)
insight: 분사는 실패한 사업을 떼어내는 일이 아니다. 지분은 그대로 두고, 그 사업을 막고 있던 '모회사라는 지붕'을 걷어내는 선택이다.
misconception: 사업을 떼어내는 건 실패를 인정하는 일이고, 한 지붕 아래 있을수록 언제나 더 강하다.

sources.text: PepsiCo, 1997 spin-off of its restaurant businesses (Pizza Hut, Taco Bell, KFC) as Tricon Global Restaurants; Yum! Brands corporate history (renamed 2002)
eBay Inc., press releases on the separation of PayPal (completed July 2015)
레스토랑 그룹, 예약 소프트웨어, 프로젝트 관리 소프트웨어 사례는 설명용 가상 예시

factChecks.note: PepsiCo 레스토랑 부문 분사는 1997년 발표·완료(10월경), 신설 회사명 Tricon Global Restaurants, 2002년 Yum! Brands로 개명. 게시 전 Yum! Brands 공식 연혁으로 연도와 사명을 다시 확인하세요.
"경쟁 레스토랑 체인이 경쟁사를 소유한 Pepsi의 음료를 꺼렸다"는 분사 이유는 자주 인용되지만 1차 출처(당시 PepsiCo 발표, 언론 보도)로 확인이 필요합니다. 카드에는 "one commonly cited reason"으로 완화해 적었습니다.
eBay의 PayPal 분사는 2014년 9월 발표, 2015년 7월 완료. "독립 후 eBay의 경쟁사와도 더 자유롭게 제휴할 수 있었다"는 일반적 설명으로만 적었고 구체적 제휴사나 수치는 넣지 않았습니다. 게시 전 eBay 보도자료로 확인하세요.
분사에서 기존 주주가 신설 회사 주식을 받는다는 설명은 일반적인 방식이며, 국가별 법률·세무 내용은 다루지 않았습니다.

cards.title: Why PepsiCo let go of Pizza Hut, Taco Bell and KFC
body: In 1997, PepsiCo owned three of the world's biggest restaurant chains. It didn't sell them. It moved them into a new, separate company and gave its own shareholders shares in it.
The restaurants left the building. The owners kept them. That move has a name, and it isn't about failure.

image.label: A big house with one wing becoming its own house
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 큰 집 한 채에서 한쪽 별채가 분리되어 옆에 독립된 집으로 서는 장면. 두 집 모두 같은 열쇠고리(같은 주인)에 걸린 열쇠로 표현. 실제 기업 로고나 상표는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Your sauce is too good for one owner.
body: You own a group of 12 restaurants. Your kitchen also makes a hot sauce guests love. Other restaurants want to stock it, but many won't buy from a rival group. And every year the sauce team fights the restaurants for the same budget.
You believe the sauce has a big future. What do you do?

options.text: Keep it inside and give the sauce team a bigger budget
options.feedback: More money helps, but it doesn't remove the real block: rival restaurants still see the sauce as your product. And the budget fight returns next year.

options.text: Sell the sauce business to a large food company
options.feedback: This removes the rival problem and brings in cash. But you hand the big future you believe in to someone else.

options.text: Make it a separate company that you and your partners still own
options.feedback: Rivals can now buy from an independent supplier, and the sauce team controls its own budget. You keep the upside. That's the idea in this lesson.

cards.title: A software company hits the same wall.
body: Picture a company that sells booking software to hair salons. Its team built a payments tool so good that other software companies want to use it.
But many of them compete with the parent for the same salons. Sending their customers' payments through a rival feels risky. Inside, the tool also waits behind the main product for engineers.
Different industry, same shape: a unit whose best customers don't trust its owner.

image.label: Two side-by-side scenes: a sauce kitchen and a payments app, both behind a wall
image.brief: 좌우 2분할 일러스트. 왼쪽: 레스토랑 주방의 소스 병, 오른쪽: 노트북 화면의 결제 화면. 두 쪽 모두 앞에 낮은 벽이 있고, 벽 너머에서 다른 가게·다른 회사 캐릭터들이 망설이며 바라봄. 실제 로고 없음.

cards.title: Spin-off
body: A **spin-off** turns one part of a company into a separate, independent company. Usually the current owners receive shares in the new company, so nothing is sold for cash.
The unit gets its own leaders, its own budget and its own scoreboard. The owners still own both pieces. What changes is that each piece can now make choices that fit its own business.
cards.callout: A sale ends your ownership. A spin-off ends the shared roof.
cards.softwareNote: In the booking-software case, the payments tool becomes its own company. Rival software firms now sign with an independent supplier, and the tool hires its own engineers instead of waiting in line.

cards.title: Why a unit can be worth more on its own.
body: Three things often change after a spin-off:
list: **Neutrality:** customers who compete with the old parent can buy without feeding a rival
**Its own money:** the unit stops competing with siblings for budget and can raise funds on its own story
**Clear scorekeeping:** managers are judged and paid on their own results, not hidden inside a bigger total
cards.callout: The business itself doesn't change. The limits around it do.

cards.title: Two real separations.
body: PepsiCo's restaurants became Tricon Global Restaurants in 1997, later renamed Yum! Brands. One commonly cited reason: rival chains were wary of serving Pepsi drinks while Pepsi owned their competitors. The restaurants also needed heavy investment of their own.
In 2015, eBay spun off PayPal. As an independent company, PayPal could more freely work with stores and platforms that competed with eBay.

image.label: Two timelines splitting into separate paths
image.brief: 두 개의 타임라인 인포그래픽. 위: "Restaurants 1997"에서 한 줄이 두 줄로 갈라짐. 아래: "Payments 2015"에서 한 줄이 두 줄로 갈라짐. 브랜드명·로고 대신 음료 컵, 피자, 카드 아이콘 같은 일반 아이콘만 사용.

cards.title: Separation has real costs.
body: Two companies need two finance teams, two boards and two sets of systems. Costs that were shared now get paid twice. Anything the pieces truly did better together, like shared buying or a shared customer list, is lost.
The split itself is messy: contracts, staff and data must be divided. And a spin-off doesn't fix a weak business. A unit that loses money inside will usually lose money outside too.

cards.title: Now it's a software company.
body: You run a project-management software company with three internal units. Which one is the strongest case for a spin-off?

options.text: A mobile app that loses money but might turn around with more freedom
options.feedback: Freedom rarely fixes the math. Outside, the app loses the parent's support and still has to pay its own way.

options.text: A security-scanning tool that rival software firms want, but won't buy from a competitor
options.feedback: Here the parent itself is the obstacle. Independence opens a market that is closed today, and you keep your stake.

options.text: A fast-growing reporting feature built on the same code and team as the main product
options.feedback: Growth is a good sign, but it shares nearly everything with the core. Splitting it would duplicate work and lose real shared benefits.

cards.title: Sometimes the owner is the obstacle.
body: A spin-off keeps your stake in a business while removing what holds it back: conflicts with rivals, budget fights and blurred results.
**Try it today:** for each part of your business, ask: would customers, staff or investors treat it differently if it stood alone?
